hints: Look at where sodium and sulfur sit in Period 3, and remember how atomic size changes across a period.
Sodium forms $\text{Na}^+$ by losing its outer electron while sulfur forms $\text{S}^{2-}$ by gaining two electrons, so think about what happens to shells and repulsion.
Put the two trends together: atoms shrink across the period, but cations shrink a lot and anions expand, to decide both comparisons.
walkthrough:
**Compare the atomic radii**

Sodium and sulfur are both in Period 3. Sodium is in Group 1 on the left, sulfur is in Group 16 on the right.

Across a period, protons are added and electrons go into the same shell, so nuclear attraction increases and atoms get smaller. That means $\text{Na}$ atom > $\text{S}$ atom.

**Work out what ions form in $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$**

Sodium loses one electron to form $\text{Na}^+$: $2,8,1$ becomes $2,8$. Sulfur gains two electrons to form $\text{S}^{2-}$: $2,8,6$ becomes $2,8,8$.

$$\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + e^-$$
$$\text{S} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{S}^{2-}$$

**Compare the ionic radii**

$\text{Na}^+$ loses a whole shell, so it becomes much smaller than its atom. $\text{S}^{2-}$ keeps the same number of shells but has more electrons repelling with the same protons, so it becomes larger than its atom.

Both ions are isoelectronic in electron arrangement with extra differences, but the loss of a shell dominates. That gives $\text{Na}^+$ < $\text{S}^{2-}$.

**Combine both conclusions**

Atomic radius: sodium > sulfur. Ionic radius: sodium < sulfur. This matches the row with that exact pair of comparisons.

options.A: Incorrect on both counts. Atomic radius decreases across Period 3, so Na is larger than S, not smaller. Ionic radius also reverses because Na+ loses a shell while S2- expands, so Na+ is smaller than S2-, not larger.
options.B: Half right, half wrong. The ionic comparison sodium < sulfur is correct for Na+ versus S2-, but the atomic comparison is backwards. Across the period, Na atom is larger than S atom due to weaker effective nuclear charge.
options.C: Half right, half wrong. The atomic comparison sodium > sulfur is correct, but the ionic comparison is wrong. Students choosing this forget that cations shrink and anions grow, so Na+ becomes very small while S2- becomes large.
options.D: Correct. Na atom > S atom because atomic radius decreases across Period 3 with increasing nuclear charge. Na+ < S2- because Na+ loses the n=3 shell (2,8) while S2- gains electrons and expands (2,8,8) with increased repulsion.
